title: Salute Kaomoji (￣^￣)ゞ: Copy & Paste Saluting Text Faces
meta_description: Copy and paste salute kaomoji: (￣^￣)ゞ, ( ´ ▽ ` )ゞ, the o7 salute, (｀・ω・´)ゞ and respectful, playful and soldier saluting faces to say yes sir or got it.
hero_tagline: Text faces with a hand raised to the brow, from the gamer's o7 to a crisp (￣^￣)ゞ. Tap one to copy it.
intro: In most salute kaomoji the hand is ゞ, a Japanese repetition mark whose hooked stroke looks like fingers touched to the forehead, placed on the right of the face. The shortest salute of all is o7: o is a head seen from the side and 7 is the arm bent up to the brow. Gamers use o7 to greet or say goodbye, and to pay respects when a teammate falls. The longer faces carry a mood too, from a serious (￣^￣)ゞ to a cheerful ( ´ ▽ ` )ゞ. People send them to say "yes, on it", to thank someone, or to sign off. For the 🫡 saluting face emoji, see the salute emoji page linked below.

sections.label: Classic Salutes
sections.intro: ゞ is the hand at the brow. The face beside it decides whether the salute is stiff or friendly.

sections.label: o7 Salutes
sections.intro: The keyboard salute from online games. The o is the head, the 7 is the saluting arm, and o7 o7 means a group salute.

sections.label: Respectful
sections.intro: Gentler faces for a thank-you or a sign of respect. 敬礼 is Japanese for "salute".

sections.label: Soldier Salutes
sections.intro: Firmer faces with sharp eyes for "yes sir", "aye aye, captain" and roleplay.

faq.a: o7 is a text salute. The o is a head and the 7 is an arm raised to the forehead. Players in games like EVE Online and Elite Dangerous popularised it, and it is now used for greetings, goodbyes and paying respects.

faq.q: What is the ゞ in (￣^￣)ゞ?
faq.a: ゞ is a Japanese hiragana iteration mark, normally used to repeat a syllable. In kaomoji its curved stroke looks like a hand held at the brow, so it became the standard salute hand.

faq.q: When do people use a salute kaomoji?
faq.a: Mostly to acknowledge a request ("on it"), to thank someone, to say goodbye, or to show respect for something someone did. The tone comes from the face: (￣^￣)ゞ is formal, ( ´ ▽ ` )ゞ is warm.
